contributions.statement: Do not add an RCI-style 'review your code for security issues and fix it' self-critique step unless functional tests run afterwards in the loop, because it dropped functional pass@1 from 68.9 to 48.7 (Qwen) and from 84.9 to 59.7 (GPT).
contributions.evidence: §V inference-time interventions, Table III; one sample per task; CWEval/BaxBench (no Java).
relative_to: LLMs cannot self-correct without external feedback (Huang et al. 2023)

contributions.statement: Write security requirements as executable negative or exploit tests in the verifier loop rather than as principle text in rules files or prompts: models answered 86-97% of secure-coding principle questions correctly yet produced functional-and-secure code far less often, and security prompting mostly flipped a few outcomes.
contributions.evidence: Fig. 1 knowledge 86.2-97%; Table III secure-pass@1 3.8-91.6; Security-Aware prompt 20 vs 6 flips (p=0.009) with no functionality change. Audit: knowledge and actuation are on incommensurable scales and knowledge-label noise is high, so only the direction is reliable.
relative_to: knowing a rule is not following it

reason: The SoK part restates known work, but the measurements show that self-critique breaks functionality and that principle text does not produce secure code. Both support executable security checks over prose rules.
